title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' that follow La Longue Marche. Grothendieck is working over a base scheme S with a group scheme G of GL2 type, so that a determinant det is available.
- ρ and σ are involution-type automorphisms of G, apparently given by conjugation.
- T_ρ is the torus centralising ρ, and A_ρ is a group with A_ρ → PG having kernel G_m and image T̃_ρ.
- N'_σ consists of the elements b that conjugate σ to ±σ. The 'sign' is ε_σ(b) = b^{-1}σ(b) ∈ E' (μ_2-like, so ε² = 1). The previous page showed N'_σ = N_σ when 2 is a non-zero-divisor, but not in characteristic 2.
- B'_0 is a Borel-like subgroup with T_ρ ∩ B'_0 = {1}.
- G*_{ρ,σ} ⊂ G×G×E'×E' is the solution scheme of the twisted 'loop equation' (*): αρ(α)^{-1} = ε·βσ(β)^{-1}·ε_1(μ−1).

What the page does. It defines (25): (u,a,b) ↦ (α = u a^{-1}, β = u b^{-1}, μ = det u, ε = ε_σ(b)), from B'_0 × A_ρ × N'_σ to G×G×E'×E'. It then shows the image lies in G*_{ρ,σ}:
- Since a commutes with ρ, αρ(α)^{-1} = uρ(u)^{-1}.
- βσ(β)^{-1} = u b^{-1}σ(b)σ(u)^{-1} = ε·uσ(u)^{-1}, because ε is a central sign.
- An earlier result (II) gives uρ(u)^{-1} = uσ(u)^{-1}ε_1(μ−1) for u ∈ B'_0.
- Combining these with ε² = 1 yields (*).

Next, (25) is a monomorphism. From α one recovers u as the unique section of B'_0 of the form αa^{-1} with a ∈ ΓT_ρ, using T_ρ ∩ B'_0 = 1. Then b is recovered from β = u b^{-1}.

Conclusion. (26) asserts that (25) is an isomorphism B'_0 × A_ρ × N'_σ ≅ G*_{ρ,σ}. This is an explicit parametrisation (a 'product decomposition') of the solution scheme of the loop equation. The next page passes to the projective group PG, where the parametrisation is defined only up to scalars λ1, λ2 ∈ G_m.
errors: Slip in the second line of the verification: Grothendieck writes βρ(β)^{-1} where βσ(β)^{-1} is meant (the right-hand side uses σ).

'Mono, donc iso' is not justified on this page. A monomorphism into G*_{ρ,σ} is an isomorphism only if surjectivity (every solution (α,β,μ,ε) lifts) is also known. Presumably this comes from an earlier decomposition G = B'_0·T_ρ and the analysis in (II), but the page does not state it.

Inside the scheme, u is determined by α only after identifying the T_ρ- versus A_ρ-component. The text mixes A_ρ (in the source) with T_ρ (in the uniqueness argument); harmless if A_ρ ⊂ T_ρ, but this is not made explicit.

ideas.what: Explicit parametrisation of the solution scheme of a twisted cocycle/'loop' equation αρ(α)^{-1} = ε βσ(β)^{-1} ε_1(μ−1) in a GL2-type group scheme, as a product B'_0 × A_ρ × N'_σ
ideas.modern_name: Product decomposition of a twisted-conjugacy / Lang-type solution scheme (Iwasawa/Bruhat-type factorisation)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard algebraic-group technique (Borel–Tits style decompositions); the specific equation is Grothendieck's
ideas.where_published: Only in these unpublished notes (follow-up to La Longue Marche)

ideas.what: Sign map ε_σ: N'_σ → E' (normaliser up to sign of an involution) and the char-2 subtlety N'_σ ≠ N_σ
ideas.modern_name: Normaliser/centraliser of a regular semisimple element over a general base; characteristic-2 pathology
ideas.where_published: Analogous generalities in SGA3; this specific statement unsure

deep.surprise_reason: A routine verification and parametrisation step within a longer computation on a twisted loop equation in GL2/PGL2. It is correct up to minor slips, but it contains no new idea likely to be absent from or unknown to the literature beyond the unpublished context itself.
transcription_corrections: Previous page: 'B'_0 × A_g × N'_σ' should read 'B'_0 × A_ρ × N'_σ'.
In the verification, the manuscript indeed reads 'βρ(β)^{-1}' (an author's slip for βσ(β)^{-1}); the transcription faithfully reproduces the slip.
In (25), the crossed-out target is 𝒢_{ρ,σ} (struck through with hatching) and is replaced by 'G×G×E'×E''.
'{+donc+}' is a superscript insertion under 'mono'; the sentence reads 'le morphisme (25) est mono, car en termes de (α,β,μ,ε), u est déterminé'.
